title: On Banaue terraces visit, UN chief sounds alarm on climate risks
summary: UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres warned that the Philippine Cordilleras' centuries-old rice terraces and surrounding communities face growing climate threats.

blocks.text: In a video on Instagram on Saturday, Nov. 21, 2026, UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres warned that the Philippine Cordilleras' centuries-old rice terraces and surrounding communities face growing climate threats.

MANILA, Philippines — United Nations Secretary-General Antonio Guterres warned that climate change is increasingly threatening the centuries-old rice terraces and communities of the Philippine Cordilleras.
Guterres visited Banaue, where he said he witnessed firsthand the effects of the climate crisis on one of the country's most recognizable cultural landscapes.

"The dramatic impacts of the climate crisis can be felt everywhere around the world. I have just witnessed them again here in Banaue, in the Philippines," Guterres said in a post Saturday, November 21.
The Rice Terraces of the Philippine Cordilleras are a UNESCO World Heritage site built and maintained through generations of indigenous knowledge.

"When these rice fields were built, my country did not exist yet," Guterres said in a video recorded at the site. "It demonstrates the enormous value of the cultures and civilizations of this region."
Guterres said the terraces have already suffered damage from extreme weather such as typhoons and landslides.

"Last year we had landslides in this fantastic site. This year we are afraid of drought," he said. "Climate change is having a dramatic impact everywhere, but also here in the rice fields of the Philippines."
In his accompanying post, Guterres said a "supersized" El Niño could intensify extreme weather and bring prolonged droughts that "threaten water supplies, food security and livelihoods."
He said protecting vulnerable communities would require faster climate action, including a shift away from fossil fuels, greater use of renewable energy and wider access to early warning systems.

"The only effective response is urgent climate action: ending the addiction to fossil fuels, accelerating the shift to renewables, delivering early warning systems for all, and protecting the most vulnerable," Guterres said.
He described the terraces as an "extraordinary testament" to the Ifugao communities' understanding and management of their environment. — with John Marwin Elao
